title: Principal Systems Test & Automation Engineer
description:
About Albus Health

Albus Health is an Oxford University spin-out transforming how health data is collected and used in clinical trials and drug development.

We have developed Albus Home, a contactless multisensory platform that continuously captures physiological and behavioural data during sleep without wearables or user interaction.

Although our technology includes a physical device, Albus is fundamentally a health-data technology company. Our devices collect sensor data, including audio and radar, and connect to our cloud infrastructure for remote management and data transfer. Signal-processing and machine-learning pipelines then transform this data into clinically useful measures such as cough counts, breathing rate and heart rate.

Our technology is already deployed internationally in clinical trials, primarily with pharmaceutical companies, and its use is growing rapidly.

The Role

We are looking for a Principal Systems Test & Automation Engineer to take significant technical ownership of testing and test automation across the Albus platform.

This is a senior, hands-on engineering role spanning a complex, multi-component system including cloud software and infrastructure, data-processing pipelines, signal-processing and machine-learning algorithms, connected devices and supporting applications.

A central focus of the role is testing complex, multi-stage data-processing systems, where raw sensor data passes through multiple interconnected software components and algorithms before producing the final results. You will need to understand how data flows through the system, how the different stages interact, and where data could be lost, corrupted, incorrectly processed or otherwise produce unexpected results.

We are looking for someone with strong investigative and problem-solving skills who enjoys understanding how complex systems work, questioning assumptions, anticipating failure modes and systematically identifying the causes of unexpected behaviour.

You will work closely with engineers and scientists to understand the intended behaviour of individual components and the overall system, translate requirements and technical knowledge into effective tests, and establish how to verify that data is correctly processed and transferred between stages.

You will personally design and implement automated tests, develop and improve our testing frameworks and infrastructure, and help establish an effective verification approach across component, subsystem and system levels.

This is not a traditional Test Manager role. Line management is limited, and we are looking for someone who takes ownership, stays close to the technology, and has the curiosity and independence to investigate problems and drive improvements.

Why Join Albus Health?

You will take ownership of a critical function within Albus, testing technology already deployed internationally and scaling rapidly.

You will work on technically challenging problems involving complex data flows, interconnected processing pipelines, cloud infrastructure, connected devices and machine-learning algorithms.

About the Role

Our firmware team is growing, and we are looking for a senior engineer to take the lead on core parts of it. You'll own major parts of the embedded Rust firmware at the heart of the BMS, deliver features end to end on your own and help shape how the firmware is built. Together with Stefan, our CTO, and our embedded Rust engineer, you'll take on architecture decisions and code reviews and help take us from a tested prototype to a fully certified product. The technology is proven, the funding is secured, and the foundations you set now will define how every future Anori BMS works.

Start date: from January 1, 2027

What You'll Do

  • Own, design, implement and ship firmware features for the BMS, from requirement to verified release

  • Extend our middleware and independent modules into one real-time system: their control and data flow, scheduling and how they stay predictable under load

  • Mentor other engineers on the team, lead code reviews and raise the bar for code quality across the team

  • Set and evolve the engineering practices that keep the firmware trustworthy: testing, CI/CD, HiL, coverage and end-to-end requirements traceability

  • Debug and trace on real hardware across ARM and RISC-V cores, down to interrupt priorities, the memory map and timing of individual functions


What You Bring

Must have

  • Several years of production Rust on embedded targets (no_std), including features you designed and shipped yourself

  • Experience making, documenting and defending architecture trade-offs for embedded systems

  • A quality mindset: hands-on test experience, CI and coverage as everyday tools, and code reviews with constructive feedback.

  • Critical, analytical, systematic thinking: you reason from first principles, make your assumptions explicit and challenge existing paradigms


Strongly preferred

  • Deep embedded experience incl. async Rust on embedded targets, down to the executor: futures, wakers, pinning

  • Architecture of multicore and multi-controller systems: the partition of work, data and timing across cores and controllers

  • Hands-on debugging and tracing on ARM and RISC-V

  • Knowledge of various communication protocols and stacks: CAN, LIN, BLE, LTE modems

  • Basic hardware skills: reading schematics, working with an oscilloscope, board bring-up, debugging


Nice to have

  • Formal methods for embedded software: model checking, or a proof of a scheduling or memory property

  • A background in safety-critical (IEC 61508, ISO 26262, …) and battery systems

  • Comfortable implementing numerical algorithms (filtering, state estimation) on constrained hardware

  • Experience mentoring other engineers


You don't tick every box? Apply anyway. No one matches a job description 100%. If this role excites you and you see yourself growing into it, we want to hear from you.

What We Offer

  • Work on a product with purpose that redefines the state of art: our product is a key part to enable competitive battery energy storage.

  • Work directly with the founding team on decisions that shape the company. The team is small, so your ideas will matter. A lot.

  • Challenging engineering in an industrial, but research-near environment. We bring research into the industry.

  • A modern stack and methods: Rust, MBSE, everything as code, and the best tools and techniques for the job, chosen on merit.

  • To be both supported and challenged: room to grow, and the expectation that you will.


You might be a fit if

  • You hold yourself to a high standard and don’t settle for "good enough."

  • You want to have a big say in what the Anori BMS looks like and how it works

  • You are eager to try out new tools and enjoy incorporating AI into your work to make your life easier and more productive

  • You are excited about startups and all the opportunities and uncertainties that come with it

  • You want to be an active part in accelerating the energy transition in Europe

  • You are comfortable with English as a working language

  • You are happy to be in the office most of the time because for fast decisions we need to be in the same room. We expect you to be in the office at least 3 days / week


You also want to become an Anori? We cannot wait to meet you. Go and click the apply button. Don’t be shy, we are nice.

P.S. Extra bonus if you tell us what your favorite type of tea is.

description:
Quantinuum is seeking an experienced Software Engineer in Test to join its Global Quality Assurance team. The role focuses on automated testing across Quantinuum’s quantum computing infrastructure, from cloud services to internal communications within quantum computing systems.

We are particularly interested if you have domain knowledge in either of the two following areas:

  • a good knowledge of quantum computing as it relates to Quantinuum. Both theoretical (e.g. academic) and practical (e.g. hands-on experience of tools such as Tket, Guppy or Qiskit) would be of interest. or
  • a good knowledge of site reliability engineering testing from within the organisation. Ideally back-end testing of deployment scripts including Kubernetes, Terraform and similar, experience using AWS, and understanding failure modes of web services (note: this is beyond API/UI web testing).

If you have domain knowledge, directly or indirectly related to the above please ensure you detail it clearly within the relevant box on the application form, as well as your CV.

As a team, we cover broad automated testing areas, as well as software integration and regression tests we also write automated UI, hardware and hardware/software subsystem tests. We aim to ensure, whenever possible, that the right person is working on the right task that suits their own personal skills and strengths, so whilst the team’s overall scope is large, having experience in every area is not expected or required.

You will also work with other teams to improve testability and testing practices through technical guidance, practical support and training, and contribute to the development of QA processes for major releases.

Key responsibilities:

  • Develop thorough test plans and strategies, both independently and collaboratively with relevant stakeholders; especially identifying major risks and suggesting appropriate tests and mitigations.
  • Execute test plans: Design, develop and maintain automated integration and end-to-end tests and supporting frameworks and tooling for workflows spanning multiple teams’ front-end, back-end and other components across Quantinuum as described above.

  • Review requirements and designs for testability, and work with teams to investigate defects and understand their root causes. Help develop test plans and QA processes for major releases, aligning testing with release schedules and ensuring that coverage, results and remaining risks are documented and supported by auditable evidence.

description:
Genomics England is a global leader in enabling genomic medicine and research, focused on creating a world where everyone benefits from genomic healthcare. Building on the 100,000 Genomes Project, we support the NHS’s world-first national whole genome sequencing service and run the growing National Genomic Research Library, alongside delivering numerous major genomics initiatives. By connecting research and clinical care at national scale, we enable immediate healthcare benefits and advances for the future.

Our mission is to provide the evidence and digital systems so that by 2035 genomics could play a role in up to half of all healthcare interactions, whilst securing the UK’s position as the best place to discover, prove and benefit from genomic innovations.

We are accelerating our impact and working with patients, doctors, scientists, government and industry to improve genomic testing, and help researchers access the health data and technology they need to make new medical discoveries and create more effective, targeted medicines for everybody.

Behind the Healthcare and Research outcomes, Genomics England delivers through designing, developing and operating complex healthcare software systems.

We're on the cusp of big changes with the real prospect of genomics becoming the fabric of everyday healthcare through the lifetime - from birth to old age.

Job Description

QA Engineer - Python, Automation

Join Genomics England and help us build quality through QA from the start!

At Genomics England, we use genomics, technology and data to help transform healthcare, and we’re looking for an experienced QA Engineer with strong, demonstrable Python test automation expertise and experience testing in AWS environments to help us build quality into our products from the outset.

You’ll play a key role in driving a shift-left approach to quality, working closely with Software Engineers, Product Managers, SMEs and fellow QA Engineers to identify risks early, improve test coverage and build confidence throughout the software development lifecycle.

Working as part of a product-focused squad, you’ll help define the quality attributes and assurance approaches that demonstrate a product is fit for purpose. You’ll provide an independent quality perspective while working collaboratively with Product and Engineering to ensure quality is considered throughout delivery, rather than treated as a final testing activity.

You’ll take a hands-on approach to quality assurance, helping evolve our automation frameworks, CI/CD controls, assurance practices and ways of working. You’ll also support appropriate requirements traceability and quality evidence to enable confident release decisions and meet relevant governance and compliance expectations.

This is an opportunity to apply your experience and expertise in QA to products that enable world-leading genomic research and better outcomes for patients and families across the UK.

What You’ll Be Doing

You’ll have a hands-on role in assuring product quality, including:

  • Driving shift-left quality and assurance through Three Amigos, requirements and acceptance criteria reviews, early risk identification and test design, ensuring appropriate test coverage, traceability and quality evidence throughout delivery.
  • Working with Product Managers, Engineers and SMEs to ensure product requirements and acceptance criteria are clear, complete, testable and traceable.
  • Providing independent quality assurance and technical leadership through risk-based testing, coverage assessment, release readiness, compliance activities and automation strategy.
  • Helping define and improve appropriate quality attributes and assurance approaches to demonstrate that products and platform capabilities are fit for purpose.
  • Designing, developing and maintaining Python-based automated test suites and supporting frameworks, applying the appropriate testing approach based on product and delivery risks rather than a prescribed set of test types.
  • Developing and maintaining fast and effective CI/CD pipelines and quality controls for software running in AWS, ensuring timely feedback and appropriate assurance is embedded into delivery.
  • Supporting the squad in embedding applicable quality, regulatory and compliance requirements into delivery, ensuring appropriate controls and evidence are established and maintained.
  • Investigating defects, supporting root cause analysis and helping teams identify preventative improvements.
  • Automating the setup, management and clean-up of test datasets and test environments where appropriate.
  • Clearly communicating quality risks, coverage gaps, residual risks and recommendations to Product, Engineering and other stakeholders.
  • Continuously driving quality and process improvement within the product squad and across the wider QA community.

What We’re Looking For

We’re looking for someone who is comfortable getting stuck into the technical side of QA and has:

  • Extensive, demonstrable hands-on experience with Python test automation, including designing, building and maintaining automated test suites and supporting frameworks.
  • Proven experience testing and assuring software in AWS environments, with a practical understanding of testing cloud-native applications and services.
  • Strong experience applying shift-left quality practices, including requirements reviews, acceptance criteria refinement, Three Amigos, risk assessment and test design within Agile software delivery.
  • Strong understanding of quality assurance, requirements traceability and compliance, with the ability to assess risks, identify coverage gaps and ensure sufficient assurance evidence exists to support delivery, governance and audit requirements.
  • Experience designing and maintaining automated tests for modern applications, services, workflows or distributed systems.
  • Strong knowledge of software testing principles, risk-based testing, SDLC and Agile delivery, alongside experience with Behaviour-Driven Development (BDD) and collaborative approaches to defining clear and testable requirements.
  • Experience working with CI/CD and automated test execution.
  • Experience with tools such as Jira, Xray, Confluence and Git, or equivalent test-management and software-delivery tools.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate complex issues, identify root causes and recommend appropriate actions.
  • The ability to work collaboratively with Engineers, Product Managers, SMEs and wider stakeholders while providing constructive, independent quality challenge and clearly communicating quality risks and recommendations.

Experience with some of the following would be beneficial, but isn’t essential

  • Docker and containerised or cloud-native applications.
  • Testing and assuring distributed systems and platform-based architectures.
  • Contract testing and service mocking, using tools such as Pact or WireMock.
  • Security, vulnerability, performance, accessibility and other non-functional testing and assurance.
  • Experience working within a regulated environment, including familiarity with relevant healthcare and medical software standards such as IEC 62304, ISO 13485 and DCB0129.
  • Experience producing or reviewing traceability and assurance evidence supporting audit, compliance or regulatory expectations.

Qualifications

No specific qualifications are required. Relevant QA or software testing certifications are desirable but not essential. What really matters most is strong, demonstrable commercial experience as a QA Engineer, alongside being highly experienced in hands-on Python test automation and testing in AWS environments

Additional Information

Salary From: £53,700

Closing Date: Sunday 29th November @ 23:00 (UK time)

Right to work: we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Being an integral part of such a meaningful mission is extremely rewarding in itself, but in order to support our people, we’re continually improving our benefits package. We pride ourselves on investing in our people and supporting them to achieve their career goals, as well as offering a benefits package including:

  • Generous Leave: 30 days’ holiday, plus bank holidays, plus additional leave for long service, and also the option to apply for up to 30 days of remote working abroad annually (approval required).
  • Family-Friendly: Blended working arrangements, flexible working, enhanced maternity, paternity and shared parental leave benefits.
  • Pension & Financial: Defined contribution pension (Genomics England double-matches up to 10%, however you can contribute more if you wish), Life Assurance (3x salary), an Electric Vehicle salary sacrifice scheme and a Give As You Earn scheme.
  • Learning & Development: Individual learning budgets, support for training and certifications, and reimbursement for one annual professional subscription (approval required).
  • Recognition & Rewards: Employee recognition programme and referral scheme.
  • Health & Wellbeing: Subsidised gym membership, a free Headspace account, and access to an Employee Assistance Programme, eye tests, flu jabs.

Equal opportunities and our commitment to a diverse and inclusive workplace

Genomics England is actively committed to providing and supporting an inclusive environment that promotes equity, diversity and inclusion best practice both within our community and in any other area where we have influence. We are proud of our diverse community where everyone can come to work and feel welcomed and treated with respect regardless of any disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, religion, sexual orientation, or social background.

Genomics England’s policies of non-discrimination and equity and will be applied fairly to all people, regardless of age, disability, gender identity or reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, being pregnant or recently becoming a parent, race, religion or beliefs, sex or sexual orientation, length of service, whether full or part-time or employed under a permanent or a fixed-term contract or any other relevant factor.

Genomics England does not tolerate any form of discrimination, harassment, victimisation or bullying at work. Such behaviour undermines our mission and core values and diminishes the dignity, respect and integrity of all parties. Our People policies outline our commitment to inclusivity.

We aim to remove barriers in our recruitment processes and to be flexible with our interview processes. Should you require any adjustments that may help you to fully participate in the recruitment process, we encourage you to discuss this with us.

Culture

We have four key behaviours that represent what we would like Genomics England to feel like and the culture we want to encourage, in order for us to achieve our mission. These behaviours help us all work well together, deliver on our outcomes, celebrate our successes and share feedback with each other. You can read about these and other aspects of our culture here Culture | Genomics England

Blended working model

Genomics England operates a blended working model as we know our people appreciate the flexibility that hybrid working can bring. We expect most people to come into the office a minimum of 2 times each month. However, this will vary according to role and will be agreed with your team leader. There is no expectation that people will return to the office full time unless they want to, however, some of our roles require full time on site attendance e.g., lab teams, reception team.

Our teams and squads have, and will continue to reflect on what works best for them to work together successfully and have the freedom to design working patterns to suit, beyond the minimum. Our office locations are: Canary Wharf, Cambridge and Leeds.

Onboarding background checks

As part of our recruitment process, all successful candidates are subject to a Standard Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check. We therefore require applicants to disclose any previous offences at point of application, as some unspent convictions may mean we are unable to proceed with your application due to the nature of our work in healthcare.
